headline: Voters reject tax proposal tied to plans for Stars' new arena
take:
ESPN reports that Texas voters rejected a proposal to authorize taxes to help pay off $700 million in bonds for a proposed $3 billion development that includes an arena for the Stars.

None of this changes anything on the ice for Dallas, and our numbers say the team is in good shape. The Stars are 9-5-1 with 19 points through 15 games. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and Dallas has taken 52.5% of them so far this season, which means they are creating a bit more than they allow. At 5-on-5 that share is 52%, so it isn't a power-play mirage. The penalty kill allows 0.54 expected goals per game, a strong figure, while the power play generates 0.71. The gap between results and process is worth noting. Dallas has scored 2.5 fewer goals than expected, but goalies have saved 6.1 more goals than expected, so goaltending is holding up the record while the shooting regresses upward.
